question: Which of the five has been most explicit about serving mass-affluent clients, and what exactly have they said?

cells.label: fact

items.text: Schwab's Investor Services segment offers several relationship/service models for clients with substantial wealth needs: Schwab Private Client Services for clients with $1 million to $10 million in qualifying assets, and Schwab Private Wealth Services for clients with more than $10 million, providing enhanced, relationship-based experiences including dedicated service teams, specialized expertise, expedited processing, pricing advantages, and access to exclusive product offerings.
items.quote: For clients with more substantial needs, Schwab Private Client Services™ (for clients with $1 million to $10 million in qualifying assets) and Schwab Private Wealth Services™ (for clients with more than $10 million) provide enhanced, relationship-based experiences including dedicated service teams, specialized expertise, expedited processing, pricing advantages, and access to exclusive product offerings.

items.text: Schwab offers advisory solutions, including discretionary and non-discretionary services, with minimum investments starting at $5,000; its flagship program Schwab Wealth Advisory provides a dedicated Wealth Advisor supported by a team offering financial planning, specialized support, and customized portfolio management.
items.quote: Schwab offers a comprehensive suite of advisory solutions, including both discretionary and non-discretionary services, with minimum investments starting at $5,000. Our flagship program, Schwab Wealth Advisory™, provides a dedicated Wealth Advisor supported by a team of professionals offering financial planning, specialized support, and customized portfolio management.

items.text: Schwab serves a broad spectrum of individual investors, supporting newer investors with accessible products such as Schwab Stock Slices and the Schwab Starter Kit alongside trading capabilities, advisory solutions, and educational resources.
items.quote: Through the Retail Investor business unit, Schwab serves a broad spectrum of individual investors, ranging from those just beginning their investing journey to clients with substantial and complex wealth management needs. We support newer investors with accessible products such as Schwab Stock Slices® and the Schwab Starter Kit®, alongside a comprehensive set of trading capabilities, advisory solutions, and educational resources.

items.text: Schwab's wealth offer gives clients access to financial planning, full-service advice, tax, trust, and estate services, tax-aware strategies, and more, per CEO Rick Wurster.
items.quote: With our wealth offer, clients can access financial planning, full-service advice, tax, trust, and estate services, tax-aware strategies, and more.

items.text: Schwab launched a discretionary version of its full-service wealth management capability (Schwab Wealth Advisory) and broadly rolled out its retail alternatives platform to eligible clients, per CEO Rick Wurster.
items.quote: We launched a discretionary version of our full-service wealth management capability, an important step in meeting the holistic needs of our clients. This quarter, we also broadly rolled out our retail alternatives platform to our eligible clients.

items.text: Schwab raised the minimum account size for clients referred to RIAs to $5 million (up from $2 million) effective January 2027, and raised the AUM threshold for firms entering the Schwab Advisor Network to at least $500 million (up from $250 million).
items.quote: In August, the firm told RIAs it was raising the minimum account size for clients to be referred to $5 million at the beginning of 2027, up from $2 million. In addition, Schwab raised the assets-under-management threshold for firms entering the Schwab Advisor Network to at least $500 million, up from $250 million.

cells.reason: Passages describe specific products, services, and fee/minimum thresholds (Private Client Services tiers, $5,000 advisory minimum, $5 million referral threshold) that Schwab offers to affluent and higher-net-worth clients, which is what the sub-question asks.
